dishes.name: Jerk Chicken
dishes.desc: Chicken marinated in scotch bonnet, allspice, thyme and scallion, then smoked over pimento wood at roadside jerk centres.

dishes.name: Ackee and Saltfish
dishes.desc: National dish of boiled ackee fruit sautéed with salt cod, onions, tomato and scotch bonnet, eaten for breakfast.

dishes.name: Curry Goat
dishes.desc: Goat meat marinated in Jamaican curry powder and scotch bonnet, slow-stewed with potatoes and served with rice at parties.

dishes.name: Oxtail Stew
dishes.desc: Oxtail browned and braised with butter beans, allspice, thyme and scotch bonnet until gelatinous, served with rice and peas.

dishes.name: Rice and Peas
dishes.desc: Rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans, thyme, scallion and a whole scotch bonnet, the classic Sunday side.

dishes.name: Jamaican Patty
dishes.desc: Flaky turmeric-yellow pastry turnover filled with spiced minced beef, chicken or vegetables, often eaten inside coco bread.

dishes.name: Festival
dishes.desc: Slightly sweet, elongated fried dumpling of cornmeal and flour, served alongside jerk meats and fried fish.

dishes.name: Escovitch Fish
dishes.desc: Whole fried fish topped with a vinegary pickle of onions, carrots, chayote and scotch bonnet peppers.

dishes.name: Callaloo
dishes.desc: Amaranth leaves steamed with onion, tomato, thyme and scotch bonnet, eaten as a breakfast side, sometimes with saltfish.

dishes.name: Bammy
dishes.desc: Flat round cassava bread soaked in coconut milk and fried, traditionally served with escovitch fish.

dishes.name: Rum Cake
dishes.desc: Dark, dense Christmas and wedding cake of dried fruit soaked for months in rum and red wine, coloured with burnt sugar.

dishes.name: Rum Punch
dishes.desc: Mix of Jamaican overproof rum, lime juice, sugar syrup and fruit juices, following the 'one sour, two sweet' rhyme.

dishes.name: Jerk Pork
dishes.desc: Pork shoulder rubbed with a fiery scotch bonnet, allspice and scallion marinade and smoked over pimento wood, a Boston Bay speciality.

dishes.name: Stew Peas
dishes.desc: Red kidney beans stewed with salted pig's tail or beef, coconut milk and small flour dumplings called spinners, served over rice.

dishes.name: Mannish Water
dishes.desc: Goat-head and offal soup with green bananas, yam and dumplings, served at celebrations and reputed to be an aphrodisiac.

dishes.name: Hard Dough Bread
dishes.desc: Dense, slightly sweet white sandwich loaf of Chinese-Jamaican origin, eaten buttered, toasted or with fried fish.

dishes.name: Bulla Cake
dishes.desc: Flat round spiced cake of molasses, ginger and nutmeg, commonly eaten as a snack with cheese or avocado.

dishes.name: Gizzada
dishes.desc: Small open tart with a pinched pastry crust filled with grated coconut cooked with brown sugar, ginger and nutmeg.

dishes.name: Sorrel Drink
dishes.desc: Deep-red Christmas drink of steeped hibiscus sepals with ginger, pimento and sugar, often spiked with rum.

dishes.name: Blue Mountain Coffee
dishes.desc: Mild, highly prized arabica coffee grown in the misty Blue Mountains of eastern Jamaica.

dishes.name: Brown Stew Chicken
dishes.desc: Chicken browned in caramelised sugar and braised with onions, peppers, tomato, thyme and scotch bonnet into a rich gravy.

dishes.name: Fried Dumplings
dishes.desc: Round fried dough balls of flour, salt and butter, crisp outside and fluffy inside, eaten with ackee and saltfish at breakfast.

dishes.name: Run Down
dishes.desc: Mackerel or salt fish simmered in thick reduced coconut milk with onion, thyme and scotch bonnet, served with green bananas.

dishes.name: Coco Bread
dishes.desc: Soft, folded, slightly sweet coconut-milk bread roll, classically split open to sandwich a beef patty.

dishes.name: Pepper Shrimp
dishes.desc: Shrimp boiled with Scotch bonnet peppers and spices, sold in bags along the road at Middle Quarters.

dishes.name: Bun and Cheese
dishes.desc: Dark spiced Easter bun with dried fruit, sliced and sandwiched with processed cheese.

dishes.name: Jamaican Ginger Beer
dishes.desc: Fiery homemade drink of grated ginger, lime and sugar, served at Christmas with sorrel.

dishes.name: Ropa Vieja
dishes.desc: National dish of shredded flank steak stewed in tomato sofrito with peppers, onions and olives, served with rice and beans.

dishes.name: Cubano Sandwich
dishes.desc: Pressed sandwich on Cuban bread with roast pork, ham, Swiss cheese, pickles and mustard, iconic in Havana, Tampa and Miami.

dishes.name: Moros y Cristianos
dishes.desc: Black beans and white rice cooked together in one pot with sofrito, cumin and bay leaf.

dishes.name: Lechón Asado
dishes.desc: Whole pig or pork shoulder marinated in sour-orange mojo and slow-roasted, the centrepiece of Nochebuena (Christmas Eve).

dishes.name: Tostones
dishes.desc: Green plantain slices fried, smashed flat and fried again until crisp, sprinkled with salt or dipped in garlic mojo.

dishes.name: Vaca Frita
dishes.desc: Shredded flank steak marinated in lime and garlic, then pan-fried until crisp with plenty of onions.

dishes.name: Picadillo
dishes.desc: Ground beef hash cooked in tomato sofrito with olives, raisins and capers, served over white rice.

dishes.name: Yuca con Mojo
dishes.desc: Boiled cassava drenched in mojo, a sauce of sour orange, garlic and hot olive oil, a classic holiday side.

dishes.name: Tamal Cubano
dishes.desc: Fresh ground corn mixed with pork and sofrito, wrapped in corn husks and boiled.

dishes.name: Café Cubano
dishes.desc: Strong espresso sweetened while brewing by whipping sugar into a foamy 'espumita', served in tiny cups.

dishes.name: Flan de Leche
dishes.desc: Baked custard of eggs with condensed and evaporated milk under a layer of dark caramel.

dishes.name: Arroz con Pollo
dishes.desc: Chicken and rice cooked with sofrito, beer, saffron or annatto and peas, garnished with roasted red peppers.

dishes.name: Frituras de Malanga
dishes.desc: Crispy fritters of grated malanga root with garlic and parsley, served as a snack or appetiser.

dishes.name: Pastelitos de Guayaba
dishes.desc: Flaky puff-pastry turnovers filled with guava paste, often with cream cheese, eaten with café cubano.

dishes.name: Mojito
dishes.desc: Highball of white rum, sugar, lime juice, fresh mint and soda water, originating in Havana.

dishes.name: Boliche
dishes.desc: Eye-of-round beef roast stuffed with chorizo or ham, browned and braised in sofrito and sour-orange sauce.

dishes.name: Congrí
dishes.desc: Rice cooked with red kidney beans and pork in sofrito, typical of eastern Cuba as congrí oriental.

dishes.name: Croquetas Cubanas
dishes.desc: Breaded, deep-fried cylinders of thick béchamel with ground ham or chicken, sold at bakeries and coffee windows.

dishes.name: Tres Leches Cubano
dishes.desc: Sponge cake soaked in evaporated, condensed and whole milk, topped with meringue or whipped cream.

dishes.name: Natilla
dishes.desc: Stovetop custard of milk, egg yolks, sugar, lemon peel and cinnamon, served chilled.

dishes.name: Medianoche
dishes.desc: Pressed sandwich like the Cubano but on soft, sweet egg bread, named for late-night eating in Havana nightclubs.

dishes.name: Daiquirí
dishes.desc: Cocktail of white rum, lime juice and sugar, named after a beach near Santiago de Cuba and perfected in Havana bars.

dishes.name: Cuba Libre
dishes.desc: Highball of rum, cola and lime juice, said to date from Cuba's 1898 War of Independence.

dishes.name: Pan Cubano
dishes.desc: Long white loaf enriched with lard, with a thin crisp crust split by a palm-frond strip, the base of Cuban sandwiches.

dishes.name: Ajiaco Cubano
dishes.desc: Hearty stew of pork, beef or chicken with malanga, yuca, corn, plantain and boniato, seen as a symbol of Cuban identity.

dishes.name: Bistec de Palomilla
dishes.desc: Thin sirloin steak marinated in garlic, lime and sour orange, pan-fried and smothered in onions.

dishes.name: Plátanos Maduros
dishes.desc: Ripe sweet plantains fried until caramelised, served with nearly every Cuban meal.

dishes.name: Mofongo
dishes.desc: Fried green plantains mashed in a wooden pilón with garlic and pork cracklings, often stuffed with seafood or meat.

dishes.name: Pasteles
dishes.desc: Christmas parcels of grated green banana and root-vegetable masa filled with pork, wrapped in banana leaves and boiled.

dishes.name: Arroz con Gandules
dishes.desc: Rice cooked with pigeon peas, sofrito, pork and olives, the national dish served at every holiday table.

dishes.name: Alcapurrias
dishes.desc: Torpedo-shaped fritters of green banana and yautía dough stuffed with seasoned beef or crab, sold at Piñones beach kiosks.

dishes.name: Pernil
dishes.desc: Slow-roasted pork shoulder marinated in garlic, oregano and adobo with crisp crackling skin, a Christmas staple.

dishes.name: Lechón Asado (PR)
dishes.desc: Whole pig spit-roasted over charcoal, famously served at roadside lechoneras along the Ruta del Lechón in Guavate.

dishes.name: Tripleta
dishes.desc: Hefty sandwich of three meats, typically steak, ham and roast pork, with potato sticks, cabbage and sauces, sold from food trucks.

dishes.name: Bacalaítos
dishes.desc: Thin, crispy, flat salt cod fritters made from a loose flour batter, a classic beach-kiosk snack.

dishes.name: Tembleque
dishes.desc: Wobbly coconut milk and cornstarch pudding dusted with cinnamon, served at Christmas.

dishes.name: Empanadillas
dishes.desc: Fried half-moon turnovers of wheat dough filled with seasoned beef, chicken, crab or pizza filling.

dishes.name: Piraguas
dishes.desc: Pyramid-shaped shaved ice drenched in tropical fruit syrups, sold from pushcarts.

dishes.name: Coquito
dishes.desc: Christmas drink of coconut milk, condensed milk, rum, cinnamon and nutmeg, served chilled.

dishes.name: Asopao
dishes.desc: Soupy rice stew of chicken or shrimp cooked with sofrito, olives and capers.

dishes.name: Sorullos
dishes.desc: Fried sticks of sweetened cornmeal, sometimes filled with cheese, dipped in mayoketchup.

dishes.name: Pionono
dishes.desc: Ripe plantain strips rolled into a ring around seasoned ground beef, dipped in egg batter and fried.

dishes.name: Pinchos
dishes.desc: Grilled skewers of chicken or pork brushed with barbecue sauce and served with bread, sold at roadside stands.

dishes.name: Mallorca Sandwich
dishes.desc: Sweet spiral egg bun dusted with powdered sugar, griddled with ham, cheese and egg for breakfast.

dishes.name: Quesitos
dishes.desc: Twisted puff-pastry pastries filled with sweetened cream cheese and glazed with syrup, eaten with coffee.

dishes.name: Flan de Queso
dishes.desc: Dense custard flan made with cream cheese, eggs and condensed milk under a caramel layer.

dishes.name: Tostones Rellenos
dishes.desc: Cup-shaped fried green plantains filled with shrimp, crab, ground beef or chicken.

dishes.name: Jibarito
dishes.desc: Sandwich using flattened fried green plantains instead of bread, filled with steak, cheese, lettuce, tomato and garlic mayo.

dishes.name: Arroz con Dulce
dishes.desc: Christmas rice pudding cooked with coconut milk, ginger, cinnamon, cloves and raisins.

dishes.name: Pastelón
dishes.desc: Lasagna-like casserole of sweet ripe plantain slices layered with seasoned ground beef and cheese.

dishes.name: Piña Colada
dishes.desc: Blended cocktail of rum, coconut cream and pineapple juice, Puerto Rico's national drink.

dishes.name: La Bandera Dominicana
dishes.desc: Everyday lunch plate of white rice, stewed red beans and stewed meat, usually with salad and fried plantain.

dishes.name: Sancocho
dishes.desc: Thick holiday stew of several meats with yuca, yautía, plantain and corn, served with white rice and avocado.

dishes.name: Mangú
dishes.desc: Boiled green plantains mashed with butter and topped with vinegar-pickled red onions, eaten for breakfast.

dishes.name: Tostones (Dominican)
dishes.desc: Twice-fried smashed green plantain slices, the standard side for fried chicken, fish and meat.

dishes.name: Chicharrón de Pollo
dishes.desc: Bite-sized bone-in chicken pieces marinated in lime, oregano and soy sauce, dusted with flour and deep-fried.

dishes.name: Yaniqueque
dishes.desc: Thin, crispy fried dough discs sold at beaches, the Dominican take on the johnnycake.

dishes.name: Pastelón
dishes.desc: Casserole of mashed or sliced ripe plantain layered with seasoned ground beef and cheese, baked until golden.

dishes.name: Locrio
dishes.desc: One-pot rice cooked with chicken, salami, sausage or smoked herring in tomato sofrito, a Dominican cousin of paella.

dishes.name: Habichuelas Guisadas
dishes.desc: Red or pink beans stewed with squash, sofrito, cilantro and oregano, ladled over white rice.

dishes.name: Chimichurri (Dominican Burger)
dishes.desc: Street burger of seasoned pork or beef patty on pan de agua with cabbage, tomato and a ketchup-mayo sauce.

dishes.name: Morir Soñando
dishes.desc: Refreshing blend of orange juice, evaporated milk, sugar and ice; the name means 'to die dreaming'.

dishes.name: Mamajuana
dishes.desc: Infusion of rum, red wine and honey steeped with tree bark and herbs, reputed as an aphrodisiac.

dishes.name: Pica Pollo
dishes.desc: Crispy flour-coated fried chicken seasoned with lime and adobo, served with tostones at neighbourhood picapollerías.

dishes.name: Quipe
dishes.desc: Deep-fried bulgur shells stuffed with seasoned ground beef, a street snack derived from Levantine kibbeh.

dishes.name: Tres Golpes
dishes.desc: Breakfast of mangú with fried salami, fried white cheese and fried eggs.

dishes.name: Majarete
dishes.desc: Creamy pudding of fresh grated corn cooked with milk, coconut milk, sugar and cinnamon.

dishes.name: Dulce de Leche Cortada
dishes.desc: Grainy milk fudge made by curdling milk with lime or sour orange and simmering the curds with sugar and cinnamon.

dishes.name: Moro de Guandules
dishes.desc: Rice cooked together with pigeon peas, sofrito and often coconut milk, especially popular at Christmas.

dishes.name: Bizcocho Dominicano
dishes.desc: Moist, airy sponge cake filled with pineapple jam and covered in meringue frosting, the standard birthday cake.

dishes.name: Catibías
dishes.desc: Empanadas made with a cassava-flour dough, filled with ground meat or chicken and deep-fried.

dishes.name: Habichuelas con Dulce
dishes.desc: Sweet cream of red beans with coconut milk, sweet potato, raisins and spices, served during Lent with milk cookies.

dishes.name: Chivo Guisado
dishes.desc: Goat meat stewed with oregano, tomato, peppers and rum or wine, famously from the northwestern province of Montecristi.

dishes.name: Griot
dishes.desc: Pork shoulder chunks marinated in sour orange and epis, braised then fried crisp, served with pikliz and fried plantains.

dishes.name: Diri ak Djon Djon
dishes.desc: Rice cooked black in a broth of dried djon djon mushrooms, often with lima beans or shrimp.

dishes.name: Soup Joumou
dishes.desc: Pumpkin soup with beef, pasta and vegetables eaten on 1 January to commemorate Haitian independence.

dishes.name: Pikliz
dishes.desc: Fiery pickled relish of shredded cabbage, carrots and scotch bonnet peppers in vinegar, served with fried foods.

dishes.name: Tasso Kabrit
dishes.desc: Goat meat marinated in citrus and epis, boiled and then fried until crisp.

dishes.name: Legim
dishes.desc: Thick stew of mashed eggplant, cabbage, chayote and spinach cooked with beef or crab, served over rice.

dishes.name: Akra
dishes.desc: Fritters of grated malanga root seasoned with epis and chilli, a popular street snack.

dishes.name: Pâté Kodé
dishes.desc: Fried turnovers of crisp dough filled with spiced herring, chicken or ground beef, sold by street vendors.

dishes.name: Bannann Peze
dishes.desc: Twice-fried flattened green plantain slices, the standard accompaniment to griot.

dishes.name: Diri Kole ak Pwa
dishes.desc: Rice cooked together with red kidney or black beans, epis and cloves, a daily staple.

dishes.name: Lambi
dishes.desc: Conch meat stewed in a spicy Creole tomato sauce or grilled, a coastal delicacy.

dishes.name: Mayi Moulen
dishes.desc: Cornmeal porridge cooked with beans, coconut milk or herring sauce, served as a savoury side.

dishes.name: Haitian Spaghetti Breakfast
dishes.desc: Spaghetti tossed with sliced hot dogs, tomato paste, onions, peppers and spices, a common breakfast.

dishes.name: Labouyi
dishes.desc: Thick sweet porridge of plantain, cornmeal or flour cooked with milk, cinnamon and nutmeg.

dishes.name: Tablet Pistach
dishes.desc: Brittle-like confection of peanuts cooked in caramelised sugar with ginger and cinnamon.

dishes.name: Kremas
dishes.desc: Creamy holiday liqueur of coconut cream, condensed milk, rum and spices such as cinnamon and anise.

dishes.name: Pen Patat
dishes.desc: Dense sweet-potato pudding with banana, coconut milk, raisins and spices, baked until caramelised.

dishes.name: Bouyon
dishes.desc: Hearty Saturday soup of beef or goat with root vegetables, plantain, spinach and flour dumplings.

dishes.name: Marinad
dishes.desc: Fried fritters of seasoned flour batter with herbs and peppers, a Haitian street snack.

dishes.name: Doubles
dishes.desc: Two soft fried bara flatbreads topped with curried chickpeas and chutneys, Trinidad's breakfast street food.

dishes.name: Roti (Trini)
dishes.desc: Dhalpuri or paratha flatbread wrapped around curried chicken, goat, shrimp or potato and chickpeas.

dishes.name: Pelau
dishes.desc: One-pot rice of caramelised chicken with pigeon peas, coconut milk and pumpkin, a beach-lime staple.

dishes.name: Bake and Shark
dishes.desc: Fried shark fillet in fried bake bread, topped with tamarind, shadow beni and garlic sauces, famed at Maracas Bay.

dishes.name: Callaloo (Trini)
dishes.desc: Smooth stew of dasheen leaves, okra, coconut milk and pumpkin, often with crab or salted pig tail.

dishes.name: Flying Fish and Cou-Cou
dishes.desc: Barbados' national dish of steamed flying fish in a tomato-onion sauce with cornmeal-and-okra cou-cou.

dishes.name: Conch Fritters
dishes.desc: Battered and deep-fried chopped conch with peppers and onions, a Bahamian snack.

dishes.name: Macaroni Pie
dishes.desc: Baked macaroni and cheese set firm with egg and evaporated milk, a Sunday lunch side across the islands.

dishes.name: Pholourie
dishes.desc: Fried balls of spiced split-pea batter served with tamarind or mango chutney.

dishes.name: Aloo Pie
dishes.desc: Fried soft dough pastry stuffed with spiced mashed potato, served with chutney or curried channa.

dishes.name: Corn Soup
dishes.desc: Thick split-pea soup with chunks of corn on the cob, dumplings and vegetables, sold late at night after fetes.

dishes.name: Souse
dishes.desc: Pickled pig trotters or chicken feet in a lime, cucumber, onion and hot pepper brine.

dishes.name: Pepperpot (Guyanese)
dishes.desc: Guyana's Christmas meat stew darkened with cassareep, cinnamon and hot pepper, eaten with bread.

dishes.name: Cook-up Rice
dishes.desc: Guyanese one-pot rice cooked with black-eyed peas, coconut milk and assorted meats.

dishes.name: Mauby
dishes.desc: Bittersweet drink brewed from mauby tree bark with spices and sugar, served ice cold.

dishes.name: Sorrel
dishes.desc: Deep-red Christmas drink of steeped sorrel sepals with cloves, cinnamon and sometimes rum.

dishes.name: Black Cake
dishes.desc: Christmas fruitcake of rum- and cherry-brandy-soaked dried fruit darkened with burnt sugar.

dishes.name: Chow
dishes.desc: Chopped green mango, pineapple or other fruit tossed with lime, garlic, shadow beni and hot pepper.

dishes.name: Bara
dishes.desc: Soft turmeric-tinted fried flatbread made with split-pea flour, the base of doubles.

dishes.name: Sea Moss Drink
dishes.desc: Thick sweet drink of boiled sea moss blended with milk, nutmeg and cinnamon, reputed as a tonic.

dishes.name: Curry Crab and Dumpling
dishes.desc: Tobago's signature dish of blue crabs curried in coconut milk, served with flat flour dumplings.

dishes.name: Buljol
dishes.desc: Breakfast salad of shredded salt cod with tomatoes, onions, peppers and olive oil, eaten with bake.

dishes.name: Cassava Pone
dishes.desc: Dense baked pudding of grated cassava, coconut, sugar and warm spices.

dishes.name: Bajan Fish Cakes
dishes.desc: Barbadian fritters of salt cod and herbs in batter, eaten with pepper sauce or in a bread roll.

dishes.name: Bandeja Paisa
dishes.desc: Antioquian platter of beans, rice, ground meat, chicharrón, chorizo, fried egg, plantain, arepa and avocado.

dishes.name: Arepas
dishes.desc: Griddled corn cakes eaten daily, plain or filled, in countless regional styles.

dishes.name: Ajiaco
dishes.desc: Bogotá chicken soup with three kinds of potato and guascas herb, served with cream, capers and avocado.

dishes.name: Empanadas Colombianas
dishes.desc: Crispy yellow cornmeal turnovers filled with potato and beef, served with ají picante.

dishes.name: Sancocho Colombiano
dishes.desc: Hearty soup of hen, beef or fish with yuca, plantain, potato and corn cob, cooked outdoors for gatherings.

dishes.name: Patacones
dishes.desc: Twice-fried flattened green plantain rounds, served as a side or topped with hogao and cheese.

dishes.name: Bocadillo con Queso
dishes.desc: Slab of guava paste paired with fresh white cheese, a traditional snack from Vélez in Santander.

dishes.name: Aguapanela
dishes.desc: Hot or cold drink of unrefined cane sugar dissolved in water, often with lime or a chunk of cheese.

dishes.name: Lulo Juice
dishes.desc: Tangy green juice of the lulo (naranjilla) fruit blended with water or milk and sugar.

dishes.name: Tamal Colombiano
dishes.desc: Corn dough with pork, chicken, egg, carrots and peas wrapped in plantain leaves, a Sunday breakfast with hot chocolate.

dishes.name: Cazuela de Mariscos
dishes.desc: Creamy stew of shrimp, mussels, squid and fish in coconut milk, typical of the Caribbean coast.

dishes.name: Changua
dishes.desc: Bogotá breakfast soup of milk and water with poached eggs, scallions, cilantro and stale bread.

dishes.name: Lechona
dishes.desc: Whole pig stuffed with its own meat, yellow peas, rice and spices and slow-roasted for hours, from Tolima.

dishes.name: Mondongo
dishes.desc: Tripe soup with pork, potatoes, yuca and cilantro, especially typical of Antioquia.

dishes.name: Arroz con Coco
dishes.desc: Rice cooked in caramelised coconut milk, often with raisins, served with fried fish on the Caribbean coast.

dishes.name: Obleas
dishes.desc: Thin round wafers sandwiched with arequipe, jam, cheese or cream, sold from street carts.

dishes.name: Buñuelos
dishes.desc: Deep-fried balls of fresh cheese and cassava-starch dough, eaten at Christmas with natilla.

dishes.name: Natilla
dishes.desc: Christmas custard of milk, panela, cornstarch and cinnamon, set firm and sliced.

dishes.name: Colombian Coffee
dishes.desc: Mild arabica coffee from the Andean Coffee Axis, typically drunk black and sweet as a small tinto.

dishes.name: Chicharrón
dishes.desc: Thick strips of pork belly fried until the skin puffs and crackles, a staple of bandeja paisa.

dishes.name: Fritanga
dishes.desc: Sharing platter of fried meats and offal such as chorizo, morcilla and chicharrón with potatoes, plantains and arepas.

dishes.name: Pandebono
dishes.desc: Small cheesy rolls of cassava starch, cornmeal and fresh cheese, from Valle del Cauca.

dishes.name: Almojábana
dishes.desc: Soft round bread of corn flour and fresh curd cheese, eaten warm at breakfast.

dishes.name: Salpicón
dishes.desc: Chopped watermelon, papaya, banana and other fruit in fruit soda or juice, eaten with a spoon.

dishes.name: Arepa de Huevo
dishes.desc: Deep-fried corn arepa with an egg cooked inside, often with ground beef, a Caribbean-coast street snack.

dishes.name: Chocolate Santafereño
dishes.desc: Bogotá-style hot chocolate served with chunks of fresh cheese to melt in the cup, plus bread or almojábana.

dishes.name: Aguardiente
dishes.desc: Anise-flavoured sugarcane spirit, Colombia's national drink, shared in small shots.

dishes.name: Cholado
dishes.desc: Cali street dessert of shaved ice with chopped fruit, syrup, condensed milk and wafers.

dishes.name: Pabellón Criollo
dishes.desc: National dish of shredded beef, black beans, white rice and fried ripe plantain.

dishes.name: Arepas Reina Pepiada
dishes.desc: Arepa stuffed with shredded chicken and avocado salad bound with mayonnaise.

dishes.name: Cachapas
dishes.desc: Thick, sweet fresh-corn pancakes folded around soft queso de mano.

dishes.name: Tequeños
dishes.desc: Fingers of white cheese wrapped in thin dough and deep-fried, a party snack.

dishes.name: Hallacas
dishes.desc: Christmas parcels of corn dough filled with beef, pork, chicken, olives and raisins, wrapped in plantain leaves.

dishes.name: Empanadas Venezolanas
dishes.desc: Crispy fried cornmeal turnovers filled with shredded beef, cheese, black beans or cazón (baby shark).

dishes.name: Pasticho
dishes.desc: Venezuelan lasagna layered with meat sauce, béchamel and cheese, a Sunday family dish.

dishes.name: Asado Negro
dishes.desc: Eye-of-round beef caramelised in dark papelón sugar and braised in a sweet-savoury wine sauce.

dishes.name: Tostones (Venezuelan)
dishes.desc: Twice-fried green plantain slices served as a side or topped with cheese and sauces.

dishes.name: Tres Leches Venezolano
dishes.desc: Sponge cake soaked in evaporated, condensed and whole milk, topped with meringue.

dishes.name: Quesillo
dishes.desc: Dense caramel flan of eggs and condensed milk, named for its cheese-like tiny holes.

dishes.name: Chicha Venezolana
dishes.desc: Thick sweet rice-and-milk drink with cinnamon and condensed milk, sold from street carts.

dishes.name: Pan de Jamón
dishes.desc: Christmas bread roll filled with ham, raisins and olives.

dishes.name: Mandocas
dishes.desc: Ring-shaped fritters of cornmeal, ripe plantain and papelón with cheese, a breakfast from Zulia.

dishes.name: Cachitos
dishes.desc: Croissant-like bread rolls filled with chopped ham, sold at bakeries for breakfast.

dishes.name: Perico
dishes.desc: Scrambled eggs with tomatoes and onions, a breakfast filling for arepas.

dishes.name: Catalinas
dishes.desc: Soft, dark cookies sweetened with papelón and spiced with cinnamon and cloves.

dishes.name: Caraotas Negras
dishes.desc: Black beans stewed with sofrito, cumin and a little sugar, served with rice or in arepas.

dishes.name: Papelón con Limón
dishes.desc: Cold drink of papelón (unrefined cane sugar) dissolved in water with lime juice.

dishes.name: Marquesa de Chocolate
dishes.desc: Chilled icebox cake of María biscuits layered with chocolate and butter cream.

dishes.name: Patacón Maracucho
dishes.desc: Maracaibo sandwich using fried green plantain slabs instead of bread, filled with meat, cheese, salad and sauces.

dishes.name: Golfeados
dishes.desc: Sticky spiral rolls of sweet dough with papelón, anise and salty white cheese.

dishes.name: Hervido de Gallina
dishes.desc: Hen soup with yuca, ocumo, corn, carrots and plantain, a Sunday family tradition.

dishes.name: Ponche Crema
